- When sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a price spike (e.g., >80), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply downward correction of 2–5% for 2–3 days post-spike.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early forecast horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or negative; add 1–2% bias upward for first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated small positive signals (0.00–0.25), model tends to lag; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >85, reduce by 2–4% for next 3–5 days unless sentiment strongly supports.
- When sentiment is consistently low (0.00), model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias for next 3–5 days.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in first 10 days of horizon; apply smoothing or lag correction (e.g., average last 5 days) for early forecast days.
